comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> [Blomping]
> type = swift
> user = <email-scrubbed>
> key = DOB2003/09/05
> auth = https://<redacted-host>/v2.0/
> tenant = storage
> auth_version = 2

You've missed the `/v2.0/` in your connection string.

The connection string should be exactly the above with new lines replaced by , and the spaces removed. You need to put the URL in "quotes" as it has a : in.

```
rclone ls :<nick>,user=<email-scrubbed>,key=DOB2003/09/05,auth="https://<redacted-host>/v2.0/",tenant=storage,auth_version=2:<email-scrubbed>
```

If it doesn't work, double check it against the config file (I did the above on my phone so it probably has mistakes in)

```
> rclone config string Blomping:
:<nick>,auth='https://<redacted-host>/v2.0/',auth_version='2',key='HpoghC%f=pURk+rQGh5Dy9PrK8WMaq3k933Ks4z)',tenant='storage',user='<email-scrubbed>':
```

The config string here is correct but it isn't escaped for the shell.

It is worth looking at the help

```
$ rclone config string --help
```

> Print a connection string for a single remote.
> 
> The [connection strings](/docs/#connection-strings) can be used
> wherever a remote is needed and can be more convenient than using the
> config file, especially if using the RC API.
> 
> Backend parameters may be provided to the command also.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```sh
> $ rclone config string s3:rclone --s3-no-check-bucket
> :s3,access_key_id=XXX,no_check_bucket,provider=AWS,region=eu-west-2,secret_access_key=YYY:rclone
> ```
> 
> **NB** the strings are not quoted for use in shells (eg bash,
> powershell, windows cmd). Most will work if enclosed in "double
> quotes", however connection strings that contain double quotes will
> require further quoting which is very shell dependent.
> 
> Usage:
>   rclone config string <remote> [flags]
> 
> Flags:
>   -h, --help   help for string
> 

Which indicates quoting with double quotes " is the thing to do.

Hopefully this should work

```
rclone lsd ":<nick>,auth='https://<redacted-host>/v2.0/',auth_version='2',key='HpoghC%f=pURk+rQGh5Dy9PrK8WMaq3k933Ks4z)',tenant='storage',user='<email-scrubbed>':"
```

Shell quoting is complicated alas!

    rclone lsd Blomping:<email-scrubbed>

    rclone config string Blomping:<email-scrubbed>

> I got that rclone lsd command right in backup script after a half month of tweaking with it(quite litterally) including your help for the last week... It would be very hard for normal users to make inline config work if rclone config also gives them wrong output..

I'm pretty confident the output is correct. However if the input is not correct the output won't be!
